pure-announcement.rationale: This is the protocol project's README describing A2A's design — Agent Cards, JSON-RPC 2.0 transport, opacity-preserving collaboration — not a launch, release note or funding announcement.

duplicate.rationale: The nearest concepts cover MCP internals, skills format and OSV; none covers agent-to-agent interoperability between opaque agents, which is A2A's central idea.

unfalsifiable.rationale: The claims are checkable against the published A2A specification at a2a-protocol.org and six public SDK implementations.

durability.rationale: The core mechanism — capability discovery via Agent Cards and opacity-preserving collaboration between agents built on different frameworks, now governed by the Linux Foundation — is a protocol design that will still hold in twelve months even if the roadmap items shift.

actionability.rationale: It informs a concrete architecture decision — use A2A for agent-to-agent collaboration where agents must stay opaque, complementing MCP's tool-calling — and a builder can act by exposing an agent as an A2A server with an Agent Card.

atomicity.rationale: One core idea — an open protocol for opaque agent-to-agent interop — is stateable in a paragraph; the course promo, SDK list and contributing sections are ancillary packaging, not separate ideas.
